key_insight: A semi-analytical geometric method synthesizes robust single-qubit controls in tens of milliseconds rather than minutes, with comparable fidelity and robustness.
engineering_relevance: Faster pulse synthesis could reduce control-design overhead for quantum hardware while suppressing sensitivity to amplitude and dephasing errors.
method: Map quantum evolution to space curves using Space Curve Quantum Control and Frenet–Serret geometry.
Apply the Pontryagin Maximum Principle and solve the resulting boundary-value problem by shooting.
Build a reference-solution library across rotation angles and interpolate initial guesses for new gates.
evidence_signal: Across 2,000 single-qubit rotations, mean local optimization took 39.945 ms per gate after interpolation-base preparation; quantum propagation gave nominal infidelities below 10^-9 after virtual phase correction and verified robustness to quasistatic amplitude and dephasing errors.
watch_item: The reported timing excludes interpolation-base preparation, and the abstract does not establish experimental hardware performance or robustness to time-varying noise.
paper_title: Semi-Analytical Geometric Synthesis of Robust Quantum Controls
